CTC counts and CTCm scores also changed during treatment. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results - the primary endpoint (bone scan index) showed an increase rather than decrease, suggesting lack of efficacy on the primary measure. However, OS showed success in subgroups with better baseline characteristics (low pain score: 33.85 months; high global health score: 39.9 months) and partial success in subgroups with worse baseline characteristics (high pain: 9.35 months; low global health: 12.85 months). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear differential response based on baseline characteristics - patients with lower pain scores and higher global health scores had substantially better survival outcomes. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Small sample size (n=22), single-arm design with no control group, and lack of p-values make interpretation challenging.
